content.text: In Kenya, digital creators face a critical barrier: [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/usdt-payment-gateways-digital-products-infrastructure-reality-check|USDT Payment]] processors like Stripe and PayPal are either unavailable or unreliable. This isn’t just an inconvenience—it’s a blockade to your business. You’ve built [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/how-how-sell-ebooks-kenya-complete-infrastructure-guide-4|ebooks]], courses, or templates, but without a way to collect payment, your work remains locked. This guide solves that. It deploys sovereign commerce infrastructure—owned by you, powered by crypto, and immune to platform restrictions. No subscriptions. No gatekeepers. Just a stack that works where others fail. By the end of this guide, you’ll have a fully operational online store, [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/automated-ebook-delivery-after-crypto-payment-one-afternoon|COREMERCH guide to automated]] crypto payment processing, and instant product delivery. Your infrastructure. Your rules.

This post is part of the COREMERCH infrastructure series. For the complete foundation — every component, every configuration step, and the full deployment sequence — read the pillar guide: How to Start Selling Digital Products with Crypto Payments at https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/everything-you-need-know-about-automated-digital-product-3. That guide covers the complete architecture that this post builds on.

content.text: Why This Infrastructure Works When Platforms Fail: Start digital

This stack is built on sovereign principles: you own every component, and no single platform can shut you down. Hosting uses GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages—both free and globally distributed. Backend logic runs on Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script, ensuring automation without recurring fees. Orders are stored in Supabase or Google Sheets, giving you full data control. File delivery is handled via Google Drive or Cloudflare R2, both scalable and secure. Payments are processed through NOWPayments, which supports 300+ cryptocurrencies with a 0.5% fee and no KYC. This architecture is designed to withstand the exact payment and currency challenges you face in Kenya. It’s not a workaround—it’s base-layer infrastructure. You deploy it once, and it’s yours forever.
What You Need Before You Deploy

Start with your digital products—ebooks, courses, templates, or software—ready for sale. Ensure they’re finalized and packaged for delivery. Next, choose your payment network: BSC, Solana, or TRON are recommended for transaction fees under $0.10. Set up a crypto wallet to receive payments. For hosting, decide between GitHub Pages (simpler) or Cloudflare Pages (more scalable). For backend logic, choose Google Apps Script (easier) or Cloudflare Workers (more powerful). For order storage, use Google Sheets if you’re starting small, or Supabase for scalability. Finally, sign up for NOWPayments and configure your payment webhook. If you’re unsure where to start, The Sovereign Blueprint ($47) provides complete documentation and source code for all stacks.
Setting Up Your Payment and Delivery Pipeline

Begin by configuring NOWPayments to accept your chosen cryptocurrency. Set the price in USD—NOWPayments converts it to crypto at transaction time. Integrate the payment webhook into your backend logic (Google Apps Script or Cloudflare Workers) to verify payments on-chain. Once payment is confirmed, trigger the delivery script. For file delivery, upload your products to Google Drive or Cloudflare R2 and generate secure, time-limited download links. Test the entire flow: simulate a purchase, verify the payment webhook fires, and ensure the product delivers instantly. This pipeline is automated—once deployed, it runs without your intervention. If you need a pre-built solution, The Sovereign Blueprint includes templates for all components.
This infrastructure is built to withstand payment rejection and currency collapse—proven in Zimbabwe.
Going Live and Processing Your First Transaction

Deploy your frontend to GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages. Connect your backend logic and ensure all scripts are live. Test the system end-to-end: place a test order, confirm payment processing, and verify product delivery. Once confirmed, share your store link with your audience. Monitor your first live transaction closely—check the payment dashboard, order storage, and delivery logs. After the first sale, your infrastructure is proven. You’re now collecting crypto payments directly, with no intermediary. Your customers don’t need accounts—they pay, and the product delivers instantly. This is sovereign commerce in action.
Scaling Once the Infrastructure Is Running

With your stack deployed, focus on growth. Add more products by uploading them to your delivery storage and updating your backend logic. Monitor transaction fees and adjust your pricing if needed—remember, you control the entire pipeline. Use Supabase for order storage if you’re handling high volumes. Configure SPF/DKIM/DMARC for email delivery if you’re sending receipts or updates. The Sovereign Blueprint includes a scaling playbook to guide you. This infrastructure is designed to grow with you—no platform limits, no revenue caps. You’re not renting a solution; you’re building on your own land.
Do I need an LLC to sell digital products?

To start selling digital products with crypto in Kenya, deploy a sovereign commerce stack using GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages for hosting, Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script for backend logic, Supabase or Google Sheets for order storage, and NOWPayments for crypto processing. This infrastructure eliminates reliance on Stripe or PayPal, giving you full ownership and control. The Sovereign Blueprint ($47) provides complete documentation and source code to accelerate deployment.
You own every component after deployment. No platform can shut you down.
Related: How Creators Like You Are Building Sovereign Stores

Digital creators selling ebooks, courses, templates, fonts, presets, and beats often reach this infrastructure question after hitting payout restrictions or platform policy problems on Gumroad, Payhip, or Lemon Squeezy. The difference with a sovereign stack is structural: there is no platform relationship to manage, no content policy to comply with, and no payout schedule to wait on. The Edge Commerce Stack at $197 deploys the complete infrastructure in 48 hours under your own accounts. The Sovereign Blueprint at $47 documents the build process for creators who prefer to self-deploy. Both are available at https://coremerch.github.io/products.html.
Your Deployment Checklist

1. Finalize your digital products and package them for delivery. 2. Choose your crypto payment network (BSC, Solana, TRON). 3. Set up a crypto wallet to receive payments. 4. Decide on hosting: GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages. 5. Choose backend logic: Google Apps Script or Cloudflare Workers. 6. Set up order storage: Google Sheets or Supabase. 7. Configure NOWPayments and integrate the webhook. 8. Test the payment and delivery pipeline end-to-end. 9. Deploy your store and share the link with your audience. 10. Monitor your first transaction and scale as needed.
Frequently Asked Questions
Can I use this stack if I’ve never worked with crypto before?

Yes. NOWPayments handles crypto conversion automatically, and the stack is designed for non-technical users. The Sovereign Blueprint includes a NOWPayments integration guide to walk you through setup.
What happens if a payment fails or the customer disputes it?
NOWPayments verifies payments on-chain before triggering delivery. Disputes are rare with crypto, as transactions are irreversible. Monitor your dashboard to track all transactions.
How much does it cost to deploy this infrastructure?
Hosting, backend logic, and order storage are free. NOWPayments charges 0.5% per transaction. The Sovereign Blueprint is a one-time $47 purchase for complete documentation and source code.
Can I sell to customers outside Kenya?
Yes. This infrastructure is global. Customers anywhere can pay with crypto, and the product delivers instantly, regardless of location.
What if I need to update my products after deployment?
Upload the updated files to your delivery storage (Google Drive or Cloudflare R2) and update your backend logic. The stack is fully owned by you, so changes are under your control.
